nodes.speaker: Aerial
nodes.text: Eleven trays deployed. Every lunch is accounted for.{pause}Ten Bits hover in a neat ring, each balancing rice and vegetables.{pause}The eleventh carries pudding and wobbles like it knows it is precious.{pause}Aerial checks every label against the student lunch roster twice.{pause}Darilbalde arrives with chopsticks, napkins, and heroic concern.{pause}Lunch begins in twelve minutes, assuming lunch stops trying to fly.{pause}The cafeteria has never looked so prepared or so likely to orbit.

nodes.speaker: Darilbalde
nodes.text: Why are the bentos airborne when tables remain widely available?{pause}Aerial explains that the cafeteria cart lost a wheel before breakfast.{pause}The Bits can carry every tray without tilting soup onto the floor.{pause}Darilbalde says that is practical, then ducks beneath a passing radish.{pause}One tray rotates to face him with three intensely serious pickles.{pause}He steps left. The pickle tray steps left with him.{pause}A nearby soup cup watches this courtship without offering useful advice.

nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.text: Lunch network online. Formation stability: mostly encouraging.{pause}Rice tray three reports a soy packet trapped under its landing foot.{pause}Noodle tray six has begun broadcasting steam as a distress signal.{pause}Pudding tray eleven requests central placement and extra respect.{pause}Aerial answers each alert with the patience of a tiny air-traffic tower.{pause}Darilbalde asks whether the pickles have access to his schedule.{pause}The system responds by printing a tiny receipt labeled MAYBE.

nodes.speaker: Aerial
nodes.text: Every tray has a destination, allergy note, and return route.{pause}The blue labels go to Earth House near the courtyard windows.{pause}The red labels go to the workshop beside the quiet recharge nook.{pause}One silver label simply says FOR WHOEVER FORGOT AGAIN.{pause}Aerial keeps that tray close because someone forgets every Friday.{pause}The pudding Bit bumps her shoulder as if volunteering to help.{pause}Its lid rattles once, the dessert version of a confident promise.

nodes.speaker: Lunch Monitor
nodes.text: New rule: flying lunches must stay below the banner line.{pause}The lunch monitor points to decorations hanging at helmet height.{pause}Bits lower carefully until every tray floats just above knee level.{pause}Students now step over lunches as if crossing a polite river.{pause}Darilbalde carries the banner poles ahead to clear a safer corridor.{pause}The pickle tray follows directly behind him, still without explanation.{pause}Someone posts a temporary sign: PLEASE YIELD TO LOW NOODLES.

nodes.speaker: Aerial
nodes.text: The cafeteria clock says eight minutes, but the bell says hurry.{pause}A test chime sends ten Bits into automatic defensive positions.{pause}Rice becomes armor, noodles become a flexible outer ring.{pause}The pudding locks in the center and vanishes behind lunch boxes.{pause}Aerial cancels defense mode, but dessert refuses to come back out.{pause}Darilbalde calls it the safest pudding nobody can eat.{pause}Three spoons bounce harmlessly away, proving his point with excellent timing.

nodes.speaker: Darilbalde
nodes.text: My first school lunch was labeled with somebody else's name.{pause}I ate it anyway and spent a year avoiding the actual owner.{pause}Aerial says a meal should find its person, even after a wrong turn.{pause}She taps the silver tray marked for whoever forgot again.{pause}The room is noisy, but the little promise between them is quiet.{pause}Even the pickle tray backs away half a step to listen.{pause}Darilbalde decides that lunch debts should never last an entire school year.{pause}Darilbalde finally found the owner months later and learned the swapped lunch had been their first homemade meal at school.{pause}He apologized with six rice balls, an annotated map of the cafeteria, and a speech much too formal for a Tuesday.{pause}The owner forgave him before the second paragraph, but asked him to notice the lonely tables before guarding his own tray.{pause}Now he scans the workshop benches.{pause}He counts three mechanics pretending that tightening bolts is more urgent than eating.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: They wait beneath the greenhouse windows while traffic clears.{pause}Sunlight turns the hovering trays into eleven bright little moons.{pause}Aerial counts them by reflection, then counts the reflections again.{pause}The title melody returns with the Bits' soft docking chimes.{pause}Darilbalde uses a napkin to polish one pudding lid.{pause}For thirty seconds, lunch looks less like an emergency and more like art.{pause}Then a carrot rolls past and ordinary cafeteria gravity resumes.

nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.text: Warning: the south doors will open when the lunch bell rings.{pause}A strong courtyard breeze already flutters every paper label.{pause}Aerial anchors labels with peas, which works until students get hungry.{pause}Darilbalde clips napkins to trays with spare model clamps.{pause}The pickle Bit rejects its clamp and nudges closer to him instead.{pause}He writes PICKLE ROOMMATE? in the margin of the roster.{pause}Aerial underlines the question twice and adds DISCUSS AFTER DESSERT.

nodes.speaker: Aerial
nodes.text: We need a formation that survives the doors and serves everyone.{pause}A shield would lock the trays together against the courtyard wind.{pause}A roaming buffet would let each Bit seek its label color alone.{pause}The shield is safer, but students may have to chase their food less.{pause}The buffet is faster, but one pickle unit has developed opinions.{pause}Aerial asks Darilbalde to choose before the final warning bell.{pause}Around them, eleven lunches hover with the patience of extremely edible stars.

nodes.prompt: How should lunch cross the courtyard?

nodes.speaker: Aerial
nodes.text: Shield formation. Rice beside the left arm, pudding in the center.{pause}Ten Bits lock edges until the lunches form one colorful wall.{pause}Darilbalde walks behind them, reading labels through small gaps.{pause}The wind hits, the shield tilts, and every pea stays bravely aboard.{pause}A noodle escapes through a seam and waves like a victory ribbon.{pause}Aerial calls the formation stable enough for lunchtime.

nodes.speaker: Darilbalde
nodes.text: Earth House is on the left, but their rice is on the right.{pause}He rotates the shield while Aerial keeps each tray level.{pause}Students read labels through the formation like a lunch puzzle.{pause}One trades places with another to reach curry behind a fruit cup.{pause}Nobody spills, though several people eat in surprising order.{pause}The pudding remains sealed in the middle, beautiful and unavailable.

nodes.speaker: Aerial
nodes.text: Opening a dessert corridor now. Keep chopsticks below eye level.{pause}Two Bits separate by exactly the width of one hopeful spoon.{pause}Darilbalde reaches in, touches the pudding lid, and loses the gap.{pause}The shield politely rotates him away from dessert and toward spinach.{pause}Students cheer the defense system and offer tactical suggestions.{pause}Aerial records every suggestion except USE MORE FORCE.

nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.text: Courtyard crossing complete. Wind losses: one napkin, zero lunches.{pause}The napkin lands on a statue and improves its formal appearance.{pause}Aerial releases the shield into a patient serving semicircle.{pause}Darilbalde accepts spinach first to prove the system is fair.{pause}The pickle Bit remains beside him and earns a temporary place card.{pause}Their careful wall becomes a lunch line just before the bell.

nodes.speaker: Aerial
nodes.text: Roaming buffet released. Every Bit, follow your label color.{pause}Eleven trays scatter like polite birds seeking assigned tables.{pause}Rice three circles a blue backpack before finding Earth House.{pause}Noodles six mistake a red scarf for the workshop and apologize.{pause}The pudding Bit rises above the banner line to survey the room.{pause}The pickle Bit locks onto Darilbalde and accelerates.

nodes.speaker: Darilbalde
nodes.text: I am not the red table. I am one person with a lunch already.{pause}He walks faster. The pickles match his pace without spilling brine.{pause}Students begin cheering as if the cafeteria has become a racecourse.{pause}Aerial asks him to lead the tray past the correct label colors.{pause}He loops around Earth House, the workshop, and the recharge nook.{pause}The pickle unit refuses every customer and maintains pursuit.

nodes.speaker: Aerial
nodes.text: The other ten Bits locate their tables and request landing clearance.{pause}Students hold out hands like tiny runway crews with chopsticks.{pause}Curry, fruit, noodles, and rice settle without a single collision.{pause}Only Darilbalde continues jogging beneath three determined pickles.{pause}Aerial checks the roster and finds his lunch has no pickle portion.{pause}The tray may not be confused. It may simply like him.

nodes.speaker: Darilbalde
nodes.text: Fine. Temporary docking permission, but no touching my dessert.{pause}The pickle tray lands beside his lunch and powers down at once.{pause}A tiny label under the plate reads SPARE SIDE DISH - SHARE KINDLY.{pause}Darilbalde gives one pickle to the student who forgot lunch again.{pause}The Bit hums with approval and moves its place card closer to his.{pause}The roaming buffet becomes seated lunch just before the bell.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: The main tune returns as trays settle across the courtyard.{pause}Aerial counts eleven Bits, then notices only ten lunches being eaten.{pause}The silver FORGOT AGAIN tray still hovers beside the greenhouse.{pause}Its intended student is absent, and the roster lists no classroom.{pause}Darilbalde checks the library, workshop, and recharge nook schedule.{pause}Someone is missing lunch, even though every tray arrived.

nodes.speaker: Lunch Monitor
nodes.text: One student volunteered to repair the broken cafeteria cart.{pause}They skipped the bell to finish before tomorrow's breakfast.{pause}The maintenance bay sits beyond the windy service walkway.{pause}Aerial attaches the silver tray to her last free Bit.{pause}Darilbalde packs half his napkins and two very cooperative pickles.{pause}They leave the noisy courtyard for the quiet end of school.

nodes.speaker: Aerial
nodes.text: The service walkway is narrow and lined with stacked chair legs.{pause}A single tray can pass, but turning around will be difficult.{pause}The silver Bit lowers until its antenna almost brushes the rice.{pause}Darilbalde walks behind it, blocking each gust with his shoulders.{pause}Aerial follows the roster map and listens for repair tools.{pause}From far ahead comes one wrench tap, then a very hungry sigh.{pause}At the first corner, the silver Bit pauses beside a work cart covered in cooling tools and untouched tea.{pause}A mechanic waves them onward, insisting the others should eat first, until Darilbalde places a rice parcel directly beside the wrench.{pause}The gesture spreads backward through the formation: every Bit checks for a person, not merely an open place to land.{pause}Aerial updates the roster with grease-pencil marks.{pause}She leaves blank spaces for seconds instead of letting forgotten names disappear.

nodes.speaker: Mechanic
nodes.text: I was going to eat after the wheel stopped arguing with me.{pause}The mechanic reveals a cart wheel mounted backward and very proudly.{pause}Aerial places the silver tray on the only clear corner of the bench.{pause}Darilbalde offers a pickle, which the mechanic accepts without fear.{pause}The Bit unfolds a napkin like a tiny flag of lunchtime victory.{pause}For one minute, tools stop and everyone eats in companionable quiet.

nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.text: Delivery complete, but dessert remains in defensive storage.{pause}The pudding Bit redocks with ten others and rebuilds the shield.{pause}Every lunch has reached a student except the pudding in its center.{pause}Aerial tries voice commands, manual commands, and a respectful tap.{pause}The shield rotates, presenting twelve vegetables and no dessert.{pause}Darilbalde says this has become a matter of cafeteria principle.

nodes.speaker: Aerial
nodes.text: When I was new, I thought helping meant controlling every detail.{pause}Sometimes the Bits found kinder routes than the ones I planned.{pause}Darilbalde says plans still matter when pudding develops armor.{pause}They laugh, and the title tune returns beneath the docking chimes.{pause}The pickle Bit nudges the shield and opens a gap for one second.{pause}Aerial realizes lunch may need either trust or one final formation.{pause}She asks the Bits to report what they protected along the route, expecting tray numbers and temperature readings.{pause}Instead they signal the sleepy mechanic, the nervous student, the empty chair, and the parcel saved for a late shift.{pause}Darilbalde admits the machines have learned the important roster faster than either pilot did.{pause}Whatever final formation they choose must preserve those observations instead of reducing lunch to efficient movement.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: Students gather with spoons while the pudding shield gleams.{pause}Aerial can secure dessert as the perfect edible centerpiece.{pause}Or she can release every Bit and let the pudding choose its table.{pause}The first plan promises equal slices if anyone can reach them.{pause}The second promises motion, surprises, and autonomous pickles.{pause}The final bell rings as Aerial places her hand on the command panel.

nodes.speaker: Aerial
nodes.text: Keep the shield, but open one serving corridor at a time.{pause}She assigns students to hold bowls in a calm rotating circle.{pause}Darilbalde uses the earlier noodle seam as an access point.{pause}The shield parts exactly wide enough for one pudding cup.{pause}A spoon goes in, dessert comes out, and the wall closes again.{pause}The whole cafeteria begins chanting OPEN, SCOOP, CLOSE.

nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.text: Pudding defense converted to pudding service with zero losses.{pause}Rice trays become shelves while fruit cups mark the queue.{pause}The student mechanic rolls in the repaired cart to collect dishes.{pause}Its formerly backward wheel now points forward with quiet dignity.{pause}Aerial places the last pudding cup on the silver forgotten tray.{pause}Darilbalde awards the pickle Bit a clamp-shaped service badge.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: The lunch shield is beautiful, useful, and finally edible.{pause}Students pose around it before taking the last equal spoonfuls.{pause}Aerial saves a photo for future emergency formation manuals.{pause}Darilbalde adds a warning: dessert walls require dessert doors.{pause}The pudding melody swells while Bits blink in a perfect ring.{pause}Even the lunch monitor admits flying food can be organized.

nodes.speaker: Aerial
nodes.text: All eleven lunches delivered, shared, and safely returned.{pause}The repaired cart waits for tomorrow, but the Bits request standby duty.{pause}Aerial approves one weekly shield lunch with accessible pudding.{pause}Darilbalde keeps the pickle badge on his bag as a reminder.{pause}Next Friday, students bring spoons before anyone sounds the bell.{pause}The final pudding cup opens normally, to thunderous applause.

nodes.speaker: Aerial
nodes.text: Free-service mode. Every Bit may choose how it helps.{pause}The shield opens into eleven trays that hover around the students.{pause}Pudding circles once, then lands beside the mechanic's repaired cart.{pause}Rice trays form a low table for anyone without a seat.{pause}The pickle unit settles next to Darilbalde with complete confidence.{pause}He moves his bag. The tray moves its tiny place card too.

nodes.speaker: Darilbalde
nodes.text: You may share my table, but you cannot follow me through math class.{pause}The pickle Bit answers with a docking chirp that sounds noncommittal.{pause}Students trade sides and desserts without waiting for labels.{pause}Aerial watches the silver tray seek anyone holding no lunch.{pause}It offers the last pudding to the lunch monitor first.{pause}Freedom looks less tidy than formation, but nobody is overlooked.

nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.text: When dismissal sounds, ten Bits return to Aerial in a bright ring.{pause}The eleventh follows Darilbalde toward the residence hall.{pause}He turns around three times. The pickle tray turns around three times.{pause}Aerial checks the roster and adds TEMPORARY ROOMMATE beside its number.{pause}The roaming buffet tune follows them down the evening path.{pause}A tiny napkin flutters from the tray like a moving-day flag.

nodes.speaker: Darilbalde
nodes.text: The pickle tray takes the desk corner and respects none of my books.{pause}It wakes him at lunch time with one firm docking chime.{pause}In return, Darilbalde keeps its clamps polished and labels straight.{pause}Aerial visits with rice, pudding, and a formal roommate agreement.{pause}Clause one says SHARE KINDLY. Clause two says NO HALLWAY RACING.{pause}Both roommates sign, though one signature is a soy-sauce dot.
